text:
maria: heads-up, canary rollout of runtime v2.3.1 started at ~10:40 UTC and we're seeing p95/p99 regressions on text-gen routes. p95 now ~520ms (was ~120ms), p99 ~2.1s (was ~300ms). multiple customers hitting timeouts. ops-bot fired an alert at 10:45.

ashwin: confirmed on prometheus. Query: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=\"/v1/generate\"}[5m])) by (le))` shows spike coincident with canary start.

vince: v2.3.1 included batching tweaks and kernel selection opt (prefer_fp16_kernels=true) plus a KV eviction rewrite. Which of these could cause recompute?

maria: canary weight 10%. Canary pods show batch_size cap lowered to 64 and KV eviction mode changed to LRU-window.

safiya: CS reports payloads that used to be <500ms now >1s and some 504s — ticket INC-4122. Sequences are long (avg ~1024 tokens).

ashwin: long context + eviction change could thrash KV causing recomputes. fp16 kernel fallback could also add overhead for large matmuls.

julian: checking pod metrics — canary runtime processes have high CPU sys and stole time. top from pod:
```
PID USER   %CPU %SYS %MEM COMMAND
1234 runtime 78.5 12.3 2.1 /opt/redwood/runtime --model=gpt-xx --kv-cache=adaptive
```

maria: no OOMs in `kubectl describe`. k8s-deploy-bot confirms 10% traffic to canary.

ashwin: reproduced locally with customer's payload on v2.3.1: p95~480ms p99~1.9s. Reverting KV eviction change locally returns p95~130ms.

vince: that strongly implicates the KV eviction rewrite; it likely forces more recomputation when contexts exceed the eviction window.

safiya: we need mitigations fast — customers seeing 504s. Recommend immediate rollback of canary and open an incident.

maria: agree. k8s-deploy-bot, rollback canary to v2.3.0 and set weight 0.

k8s-deploy-bot: rollback request received. Rolling canary weight 10% -> 0%, scaling v2.3.0 to handle traffic.

ops-bot: rollback started at 10:52 UTC. oncall paged.

maria: I'll notify CS and customers of rollback and that we're investigating root cause.

ashwin: I'll bisect between v2.3.0 and v2.3.1 to find offending commit. Will add instrumentation for KV hit/miss and eviction counts.

vince: add a temporary guardrail in the deployment pipeline to block kv eviction policy changes without perf sign-off.

julian: post-rollback smoke checks: p95 back to ~130ms, p99 ~320ms within 10 minutes. Looks like rollback effective.

maria: good. Next steps: 1) ashwin to bisect & produce a minimal repro + PR with fix and perf tests, 2) julian to add perf harness and long-seq traces to CI for KV/batching changes, 3) vince to add pipeline guardrails, 4) safiya to coordinate customer comms and ticket updates.

ashwin: bisect points to commit `b3f4a1` that adjusted eviction window logic in `kv_manager.cpp`. Reverting that block locally fixes p99. Will open PR with patch + regression test that runs long-seq workload and asserts p95/p99 thresholds.

julian: found kernel logs flagging `kernel_fallback: fp16->fp32 on op matmul` when seq_len > 768. Could be interacting with eviction causing different op size patterns. Add to diagnostic logs.

safiya: CS asked for ETA. We can say rollback completed and we're working on a fix; tentative ETA for patch 48-72 hours. I'll update customers.

maria: create incident page and postmortem template. Also draft a runbook for latency regressions including quick rollback steps, who to ping, and customer notification templates.

vince: require perf/unit that exercises long-seq traces measuring p95/p99 on any PR touching kv/batching/kernel selection. Add to CI gating.

ops-bot: rollback finished at 10:58 UTC. production traffic back to v2.3.0.

maria: thanks all. Assign follow-ups: ashwin (root-cause PR), julian (perf tests & logs), vince (pipeline & CI guardrails), safiya (customer comms). I'll keep the thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
